chunks: Through the same chain of narrators, it is narrated from Abu Nasr Hibatullah ibn Muhammad ibn Ibn Bint Abi Ja'far al-Amari who said: A group from Bani Nuwabakht, including Abu al-Hasan ibn Kathir al-Nuwabakhti (may Allah have mercy on him), and Umme Kulthum bint Abi Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amari (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to me that in a certain time, what was sent to the Master of the Command (peace be upon him) from Qom and its surroundings was brought to Abu (Ja'far) (may Allah be pleased with him).

When the messenger reached Baghdad and entered to Abu Ja'far and delivered to him what was entrusted to him, and bid him farewell and was about to leave, Abu Ja'far said to him: 'There remains something of what you were entrusted with, where is it?' The man said to him: 'Nothing remains with me, my master, that I have not delivered,' Abu Ja'far said to him: 'Yes, something remains. Return to what you have with you and search it and remember what was given to you.' The man left and remained for days remembering, searching, and thinking, but he did not recall anything, nor did anyone with him inform him of anything. He returned to Abu Ja'far and said to him: 'Nothing remains in my hand of what was given to me (which I have carried) to your presence.' Abu Ja'far said to him: 'It is said to you: What happened to the two Sardani garments that so-and-so ibn so-and-so gave to you?'

The man said to him: 'Yes, by Allah, O my master, I have forgotten them until they left my mind, and I do not know now where I placed them.' The man left, and nothing that was with him remained but he searched it and untied it, and asked whoever carried something of the goods for him to search for that, but he could not find any news of them. He returned to Abu Ja'far (and informed him).

Abu Ja'far said to him: 'It is said to you: Go to so-and-so the cotton seller, to whom you carried the two loads of cotton in the cotton market. Open one of them, which has such and such writing written on it, for they are on its side.' The man was bewildered by what Abu Ja'far informed him of, and went to the place himself. He opened the load that he told him to open, and behold, the two garments were on its side, having slipped in with the cotton. He took them and came (with them) to Abu Ja'far, and delivered them to him and said to him: 'I had forgotten them, because when I tied the goods, they remained, so I placed them on the side of the load so that it would be safer for them.'

key_terms.السَّرْدَانِيَانِ: Sardani garments (a type of fine fabric/cloth)
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: Master of the Command (referring to Imam al-Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the forgotten garments and the Imam's knowledge of their location?
ai.summary: This narrative from Kitab al-Ghayba highlights the Imam's knowledge of hidden matters (ilm al-ghaybah) through a specific incident where a messenger forgot two garments entrusted to him. Abu Ja'far accurately predicted their location in a specific cotton load, demonstrating the Imam's awareness of the details of worldly affairs. This event serves as a key proof of the Imam's spiritual authority and his connection to the divine knowledge that governs both the seen and unseen worlds.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 249 - Through the same chain of narrators, it is narrated from Abu Nasr Hibtullah bin Muhammad bin Umme Kulthum binte Abi Ja’far Amari that he said: Some people from Bani Naubakht, including Abul Hasan Ibn Kathir Naubakhti and Umme Kulthum Ibn Abi Ja’far Muhammad Ibn Uthman, may Allah be pleased with them, narrated to me that in a certain time, religious dues from Qom and its peripheries sent for the Master of the Age (a.s) were brought to Abu Ja’far .

When the messenger reached Baghdad and delivered to Abu Ja’far what he had brought and then bid him farewell and was about to return, Abu Ja’far said, “There is one thing remaining, which you have been entrusted with.” “Where is it?” “Nothing is remaining with me, my master. I have submitted everything to you,” replied the messenger. “Something is remaining with you. So return to your belongings and search and remember what all was given to you,” said Abu Ja’far. The messenger left and for many days tried to remember, search and think. He did not recall anything, nor did anyone who was with him, reminded him of anything. He came back to Abu Ja’far and said: “Nothing given to me remains with me that I have not brought to your eminence.” Abu Ja’far said, “It is said that you have two Sardani garments, which were given to you by a certain man,” mentioning his name and his father’s name. “Where are they?”

The messenger said: “Yes, by Allah, O my master, I totally forgot about them and I do not even remember where I have put them.” The man left and searched and opened everything he had with him and asked all he had carried something for, to look for those garments, but they were not to be found anywhere. He returned to Abu Ja’far and told him about the mishap.

Abu Ja’far said, “You are ordered to go to so-and-so, the cotton seller, to whom you carried two loads of cotton in the cotton market. Open one of them having such and such writing. The two garments are on its side.” The messenger was amazed by the prediction of Abu Ja’far and went ahead to the spot and opened the load that he had told him of and there they were: two garments on the side, inserted into the cotton. He took them and brought them to Abu Ja’far and said: “I forgot them, because when I tied the goods, they were left outside by mistake, so I put them on the side of the cotton load to keep them safe.”
